Latin word

parvus

parvus, parva, parvum

adjective; comparative minor, superlative minimus · Declension on Wiktionary

small, little; little, young (of children)

In this lexicon

  • small

    the recommended word · classical · Verg. G. 4.176: sī parva licet compōnere magnīs; Cic. Rep. 1.26: quam parva sit terra (Lewis & Short); Traupman 340; Traupman 381

  • young

    also used · classical · Traupman 410

Examples

  • dextrae sē parvus Iūlus implicuit sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs

    little Iulus took my right hand and followed his father with shorter stepsVerg. A. 2.723–724

    In the entry for small

  • parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum: ā cane nōn magnō saepe tenētur aper

    a small viper kills a huge bull with its bite; a boar is often held by a dog that is not bigOv. Rem. 421–422

    In the entry for small

  • parvus (parvulus) nātū

    young (in age)Traupman 410

    In the entry for young
